$comment: Shared authorization-conformance fixture. Covers the permission-holding rule and the authorization shape, so every SDK applies the same decision. A consumer that re-implements `allows` instead of using the SDK's is the failure this fixture exists to prevent: two implementations disagreeing about whether `panel:*` grants `panel:read` is an authorization bug, not a style difference.

rule.summary: An exact match grants. `domain:*` is a PREFIX rule: it grants every permission starting with `domain:`. A bare `*` grants everything, including a single-segment code. An empty requirement is always granted.
rule.mirrors: domains/permissions/matcher.go Matches(). A client rule that disagrees with the server is a display bug at best and a false sense of safety at worst.
rule.why_prefix_not_exact: `a:*` grants `a:b:c`, because the server compares the `domain:` prefix. Treating it as an exact pair match would hide controls the server does grant.
rule.why_bare_star_is_everything: The server treats `*` as a global wildcard. A client that denied on `*` would refuse to show what the server allows.

cases.why: The ordinary case a panel depends on.
The prefix includes the colon, so panel:* cannot reach panelx:.
The server compares the domain: prefix, so a deeper permission is covered.
The server treats a bare * as a global wildcard.
The server's global wildcard matches even a single-segment code.
Without the :* suffix the server compares the code exactly.

authorization_shape.summary: The fields every SDK's authorization read must be able to produce. A missing optional field is absent, never defaulted to a value that grants something.

menu_node.rule: An empty `permission` on a node or button means always shown; it must not be treated as a permission code that fails to match.

invariants: The server decides; this rule only decides what the client shows or hides.
A client-side allow that disagrees with the server is a display bug at best and a false sense of safety at worst.
Identity comes from the validated bearer, never from anything the caller supplied.
An unknown permission code is denied, never treated as a wildcard.
Menus are a convenience for navigation and are not an authorization surface.
